checks: A containing halfspace restricts to an intrinsic closed halfspace or the whole affine hull. Conversely, an intrinsic defining affine functional extends to the ambient space. Thus the traces used to compute depth agree. For a singleton k=1 and the only containing trace has total mass M, also the weight of its full minimal face.

In the finite-set witness lemma, an empty vertex set R containing two distinct same-label atoms also has their midpoint in P intersect conv(R)=R. That point is a nonvertex, a contradiction regardless of its label. Thus the size bound is k, with no completeness or Euclidean lattice assumptions needed for the general statement.

The finite-support construction applies to the normalized positive atomic law with closed location set P. Its strict heavy-complement cut keeps every boundary atom of a tested closed halfspace in that halfspace. A cut of mass exactly alpha is admissible. The same reasoning works for every strictly positive weight vector on the fixed P.

Each depth is the minimum of the same finite family of linear trace sums before and after perturbation. The sum of the absolute changes bounds every trace change and therefore also the depth change. Proper faces are exposed and give the exact trace P intersect F_p for an upper bound on depth. For the full face the same upper bound is the total mass.

Outside the exception the perturbation preserves total M by the zero sum of v, preserves positivity for small enough epsilon, and hence preserves the threshold M/k. The finitely many old strict depth gaps and old strict face-weight gaps remain strict with a single epsilon. For faces whose original mass equals alpha, the negative dot product with v gives perturbed mass strictly below alpha. When this family is empty, v=0 works. A perturbed center therefore had original depth at least alpha and its original minimal face had mass strictly above alpha.

The exceptional equal-mass vertices have depth exactly alpha by the atom lower bound and the exposing-face upper bound. If the number of atoms equals k and the weights are unequal, a heavy atom is a direct strict-face center. If the weights are equal and there is a nonvertex atom, its minimal face is generated by more than one atom, giving strict face mass by positivity. As an exact boundary check, the line support (0,1,2) of weights (2,1,3) with the endpoints sharing a label has alpha=3, middle-point depth exactly 3 and middle-point face mass 6.

For an affine lattice, differences of two same-coset points belong to 2L, so the midpoint lies in c+L and in Q. Completeness gives its membership in P. The free lattice group L has quotient of order 2 to its rank, including rank zero. For the graph, the midpoint formula gives actual membership in the lifted support for every distinct same-parity pair. No closure of the midpoint's label class is needed.

overlap.comparison: The stated graph bound is 2^n. Its general finite-set witness lemma plus the arbitrary same-label midpoint argument gives the stronger occupied-count Helly bound k used here. In combination with c6b7777f667984de this covers source claim :01. Neither proves a strict mass bound on a center's original minimal face.

Its proof gives the generic atomic centerpoint for closed T with a finite Helly bound and finite probability support in T. The substitution T=P and h=k covers the full nonstrict weighted depth claim jointly with bee3cc8e50a0dcea. There is no strict minimal-face assertion in that construction.

The general S-Helly measure theorem gives the same nonstrict depth bound when S=P and the occupied-count argument gives h(P)<=k. It is another route to the covered portion and has no strict face-mass conclusion.

Its equal-volume original-fiber hypothesis implies the exact midpoint identities for the original centroid graph, and it gives a mixed-volume depth estimate. The new graph specialization takes the midpoint identities as hypotheses, allows arbitrary positive atomic weights and proves strict minimal-face mass in the graph. The two conclusions are distinct.

Its equal-weight vertex exception concerns exponential-capacity equality at the ambient 2^n scale on a complete positive-fiber lattice support. It does not establish a center attaining the occupied-count depth and strict original minimal-face mass simultaneously.
